text:
alex: Heads-up — running into a regression on P99 for small streaming requests after the kernel-selection fallback landed in canary. P99 up ~25ms on our HTTP2 path. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: saw a blip in the dashboard around 03:20 UTC, thought it was noise. Can you paste the perf output? :eyes:

alex: TL;DR: host-side overhead (tokenize + parse + chunk framing) increased. Raw summary from `pprof` on one unhappy host: 
```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   samples  name
0.65s  32.5% 32.5%   0.95s 47.5%    130000  grpc.(*server).writev
0.30s  15.0% 47.5%   0.45s 22.5%     60000  tokenizer.tokenize
0.22s  11.0% 58.5%   0.35s 17.5%     44000  parse.RequestUnmarshal
0.18s   9.0% 67.5%   0.40s 20.0%     36000  stream.chunker.frame
```

alex: the interesting part is writev dominating for small responses — we probably regress because fallback model increases number of small incremental writes.

tyler: does the fallback change chunk boundaries or just inference kernel latency? I thought fallback was only kernel selection.

alex: it ends up increasing decode time slightly which exposes host framing cost. Also kernel fallback switches to smaller output-block sizes causing more frequent flushes.

sasha: can we change batching heuristics to coalesce more aggressively at the ingress? E.g., add a 3-5ms coalescing window for writev on HTTP2 when payload < 2KB to reduce syscall count.

maria: +1 on a small coalesce window. But watch latency SLO for single-request fast-paths. Maybe only enable when model latency > threshold or when downstream kv-cache hit-rate < 80%.

alex: I ran a small opt to buffer up to 4k or 4ms (whichever first) before flush in the host-framer. Local microbench: p99 drops by ~18ms, p50 unchanged. But we saw 0.3% of requests delayed >100ms in the synthetic micros (only in pathological tiny payloads).

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary cluster metrics: epoch=12, coalesce-buffer=true (experimental), kv_cache_hit=74%, p99_stream_latency=+6ms -> rolling back if error rate > 0.1%

tyler: kv_cache_hit 74% is low — maybe KV cache churn increased after the kernel change. Did we change the cache key normalization with the new kernel?

alex: yes — kernel variant suffix was appended to cache key to avoid cross-variant pollution. That doubled the effective keyspace for some workloads, briefly reducing hit-rate. We need a better stable key scheme.

sasha: proposal: keep cache key based on request prefix + prompt hash, but add a separate mapping table for kernel-variant -> fastpath compatibility. Only miss if incompatible. That avoids full keyspace blowup.

maria: good idea. Also add metric for cache-compat-miss to track how often compatibility mapping is used.

alex: action items:
- revert canary coalesce toggle if infra-bot trips rollback (done automatically)
- tyler -> implement compatibility mapping for KV cache keys (ticket #IR-2311)
- sasha -> add 4ms coalesce experiment behind flag and add histogram for delayed-fast-paths (ticket #IR-2312)
- maria -> add dashboard for cache-compat-miss and per-kernel hit-rate

sasha: small note: for gRPC / writev we can also switch to gather-write on Linux to reduce syscalls (writev already does gather but language runtime sometimes layers buffers). Need C-level benchmark.

alex: good call — I'll run a kernel-level tracer and a microbench with native writev. If we still see excessive small syscall counts, we should consider a socket write buffer that merges application slices before syscall.

maria: ping me when you have the tracer results, alex. I'll draft the dashboard tiles.

tyler: starting on IR-2311 now. ETA EOD.

alex: thanks. If anyone hits similar p99 regressions on other canaries, drop logs here and tag me. :thumbsup:
